claims.claim: Roadmap item 553222 concerns Microsoft Intune macOS custom compliance.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-01-30T00:15:33.
The roadmap describes a discovery script and JSON experience mirroring Windows and Linux custom compliance.
claims.quote: This feature will enable users to use discovery script and json file to define compliance policy to specific organziational needs. The experience mirrors Windows and Linux custom compliance experience.

claims.claim: The JSON file defines custom settings and the values considered compliant.
claims.quote: The JSON file defines the custom settings and the values that you consider to be compliant.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A platform-specific discovery script runs on policy-targeted devices and reports discovered setting values to Intune.
claims.quote: Discovery scripts are specific to the different platforms and are delivered to devices as part of the compliance policy. When a device evaluates its policy, the script detects, or discovers, the settings from the JSON file, and then reports the results to Intune.

claims.quote: Custom settings provide flexibility to base compliance on the settings that are available on a device without waiting for Intune to add these settings to the built-in policy templates.

claims.claim: Anything the discovery script prints becomes data held in Intune compliance reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Intune custom compliance discovery script output values stored report actual value macOS; "custom compliance" "script" "reports" "output" "stored". Opened custom-settings and create-custom-script; neither states that everything printed is stored in compliance reports.
claims.fix: Replace 'so anything your script prints becomes data held in Intune compliance reports' with 'and Intune displays per-setting compliance results', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/compliance/custom-settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The policy can automatically retire a device as an action triggered by noncompliance.

Replace 'before any lock or retire action' with 'before any lock or add-to-retire-list action'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/device-security/compliance/configure-noncompliance-actions, which qualifies the create-policy page's abbreviated description.

claims.claim: The schedule of the noncompliance action can provide a grace period.
claims.quote: You can configure the schedule to give your users a grace period, such as one day.
